summary: We summarize recent developments in the theory of the Benjamin-Ono equation, a well-known long-wave asymptotic model for internal waves in deep water, focusing on results obtained by means of an explicit formula for the solution of the Cauchy problem in terms of given initial data. We give a full description of this formula, and provide simple examples, with the aim of bringing it into the realm of applied mathematics. We also show how the formula simplifies further upon restriction to rational initial data. We then show how the formula and its rational restriction explain in great detail, and in a strikingly simple fashion, the asymptotic behavior of solutions of the Benjamin-Ono equation in the small-dispersion and long-time limits. In the setting of long-time asymptotics, we prove some new results related to soliton resolution yielding pointwise convergence with a concrete decay rate under the assumption of rational initial data. The first half of the paper is a stand-alone general survey and user's guide, while the appendices constituting the second half are intended for readers who want to explore the topics in greater depth, and it includes the proofs of our new results.

AI.tldr: Reviews recent theory of the Benjamin-Ono equation via an explicit solution formula for the Cauchy problem, presenting it as a user's guide and proving new long-time asymptotic results (soliton resolution with decay rates for rational initial data).
AI.motivation: The Benjamin-Ono equation is a well-known long-wave asymptotic model for internal waves in deep water, but the explicit solution formula and its applications remain largely inaccessible to applied mathematicians.
AI.method: The paper fully describes an explicit formula for the Cauchy problem solution in terms of initial data, provides simple examples, and shows how the formula simplifies for rational initial data. It then uses the formula and its rational restriction to analyze small-dispersion and long-time asymptotic limits.
AI.result: The formula explains asymptotics in a strikingly simple fashion; for rational initial data, new results on soliton resolution are proven, yielding pointwise convergence with a concrete decay rate.
AI.conclusion: The paper serves as both a stand-alone general survey/user's guide (first half) and a deeper technical treatment with proofs of new results in the appendices (second half), aiming to bring the theory into applied mathematics.

title: Endpoint Mapping Properties of Wave Operators for Schrödinger Operators in Dimensions $n\ge3$
summary: We study endpoint mapping properties of low-energy wave operators for Schrödinger operators $H=-Δ+V$ on $\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge3$. In dimension four, we prove that a zero-energy resonance prevents $L^1$ boundedness, whether or not zero is also an eigenvalue, under $|V(x)|\lesssim\langle x\rangle^{-β}$ with $β>10$. For a zero-energy eigenvalue without a resonance, we obtain a complete low-energy $L^p$ classification in every dimension $n\ge3$ under $β>n+4$. In particular, $L^\infty$ boundedness is equivalent to the vanishing of the zeroth, first, and harmonic second moments of $Vψ$ for every zero-energy eigenfunction $ψ$. The proof identifies the finite-rank obstruction and shows that the remaining eigenvalue correction cannot cancel its critical asymptotic profiles. The same conclusions hold for the full wave operators when the corresponding high-energy bounds are available.

AI.tldr: Endpoint $L^p$ mapping of low-energy wave operators for Schrödinger operators is classified, showing zero-energy resonance/eigenvalue effects on $L^1$ and $L^\infty$ boundedness.
AI.motivation: Understand how zero-energy resonances and eigenvalues obstruct endpoint boundedness of low-energy wave operators on $\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge3$.
AI.method: Analyze low-energy asymptotics of wave operators for $H=-\Delta+V$ with decay $|V(x)|\lesssim\langle x\rangle^{-\beta}$; identify the finite-rank obstruction and show the remaining eigenvalue correction cannot cancel critical asymptotic profiles.
AI.result: In dimension four, a zero-energy resonance prevents $L^1$ boundedness (with or without a zero eigenvalue) under $\beta>10$. For a zero-energy eigenvalue without resonance, a complete low-energy $L^p$ classification holds in all $n\ge3$ under $\beta>n+4$; notably $L^\infty$ boundedness iff zeroth, first, and harmonic second moments of $V\psi$ vanish for every zero-energy eigenfunction $\psi$.
AI.conclusion: Zero-energy spectral obstructions sharply govern endpoint boundedness; results extend to full wave operators when high-energy bounds are available.

title: Theoretical guarantees for stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics
summary: We prove asymptotic bias bounds for stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics in Wasserstein distance of order two. We assume that the negative log-density is strongly convex with a Lipschitz gradient, and that the stochastic gradient estimator is unbiased with an error satisfying a mean-square Lipschitz condition. The bounds are of order $h$ under a fourth moment assumption on the stochastic gradient error and of order $h^{1/2}$ under only a second moment assumption, where $h$ is the stepsize. A spiked-noise example shows that a second moment assumption alone is insufficient for a bound of order $h$ that is uniform over noise distributions with a fixed variance.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes asymptotic bias bounds for Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD) in 2-Wasserstein distance under strong convexity and Lipschitz gradient assumptions, achieving order h with a fourth moment assumption and order h^{1/2} with only a second moment assumption.
AI.motivation: SGLD is widely used for scalable Bayesian inference, but its discretization bias (difference from the continuous-time Langevin diffusion equilibrium) needs rigorous quantification. Prior bounds often rely on strong assumptions or do not clarify how moment conditions on the stochastic gradient error affect the achievable convergence rate, leaving a gap in understanding the minimal assumptions needed for sharp bias guarantees.
AI.method: The authors analyze SGLD under the assumptions that the negative log-density is strongly convex with Lipschitz gradient, and that the stochastic gradient estimator is unbiased with mean-square Lipschitz error. They derive asymptotic bias bounds in Wasserstein distance of order two, distinguishing between a fourth moment assumption (yielding order h) and only a second moment assumption (yielding order h^{1/2}). A spiked-noise counterexample is constructed to show necessity of the stronger moment condition for uniform order-h bounds.
AI.result: The bias bounds are of order h under a fourth moment assumption on the stochastic gradient error, and of order h^{1/2} under only a second moment assumption, where h is the stepsize. The spiked-noise example demonstrates that a second moment assumption alone cannot guarantee an order-h bound uniform over noise distributions with fixed variance.
AI.conclusion: The paper sharpens the understanding of SGLD bias by showing the moment conditions required to achieve different stepsize-dependent rates. In particular, order-h bias requires a fourth moment condition, while second-moment assumptions only yield order-h^{1/2}, and this gap is fundamental as evidenced by the spiked-noise counterexample.

title: Uniqueness and nonuniqueness in the disjoint data inverse problem: a sharp spectral threshold
summary: We study the inverse problem of determining a connected, closed Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two from wave observations. The sources are supported in an open set $S$, and the resulting waves are observed on an open receiver set $R$, which may be at a positive distance from $S$. We prove uniqueness up to isometry within the class of manifolds that satisfy a subcritical spectral lower bound: $\|φ|_R\|_{L^2(R)} \ge ce^{-Cλ^θ}\|φ\|_{L^2(M)}$ for every eigenfunction $φ$, where $λ$ is the corresponding eigenvalue, $θ\in[0,1/2)$, and the constants $c,C>0$ do not depend on $φ$. If a bound of this type holds also on $S$, then uniqueness holds within the class of all connected, closed manifolds. By the spectral inequality, the bound always holds with $θ=1/2$. Uniqueness nevertheless fails at this endpoint: in every dimension $n\ge 2$, we construct a pair of nonisometric connected, closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds that produce identical wave observations.

AI.tldr: The paper studies recovering a closed Riemannian manifold from wave observations with sources in S and receivers in R (possibly disjoint), proving uniqueness up to isometry under a subcritical spectral lower bound on eigenfunctions restricted to R, with sharpness shown by a counterexample at the endpoint θ=1/2.
AI.motivation: Inverse problems from wave/spectral data typically require observations over the whole manifold or in regions intersecting the sources. The authors address the harder setting where receiver set R may be at positive distance from the source set S, aiming to understand when the manifold is uniquely determined and what geometric/spectral conditions are needed.
AI.method: They analyze wave observations from sources supported in S and measured on R, imposing a subcritical spectral lower bound on eigenfunctions restricted to R: ||φ|_R||_{L²(R)} ≥ c e^{-Cλ^θ}||φ||_{L²(M)} with θ ∈ [0,1/2). Uniqueness up to isometry is proved within the class of closed manifolds satisfying this bound. They also construct counterexamples at the endpoint θ=1/2 via pairs of nonisometric manifolds producing identical observations.
AI.result: Uniqueness up to isometry holds within the class of manifolds satisfying the subcritical spectral lower bound (θ ∈ [0,1/2)). If such a bound also holds on S, uniqueness extends to all connected, closed manifolds. The spectral inequality guarantees the bound holds at θ=1/2, but uniqueness fails at this endpoint: for every dimension n ≥ 2, nonisometric connected closed n-manifolds are constructed producing identical wave observations.
AI.conclusion: Wave observations from separated source and receiver sets determine a closed Riemannian manifold up to isometry under a subcritical spectral lower bound, and this result is sharp—uniqueness breaks down at the critical exponent θ=1/2, as demonstrated by explicit counterexamples in all dimensions ≥ 2.

title: Rigorous and effective numerics for Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti maps
summary:
We make highly accurate numerical estimates of basic properties of the invariant measure for Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti intermittent maps, an archetypal slowly mixing dynamical system. We solve the challenge of precise and efficient estimation for a map with non-uniform expansion, where the transfer operator does not have a spectral gap. We do this using an Abel function, which solves the neutral dynamics, and which we can compute accurately via an asymptotic expansion.
  Our work covers both finite and sigma-finite invariant measure cases. In particular, we obtain the first practical estimates for the parameter far from zero, including the sigma-finite case. This opens the door to much deeper numerical study of intermittent dynamics than was previously possible.
  A driving motivation for this work is the upcoming proof of optimal rates of memory loss which works equally for finite and infinite invariant measure cases. No prior results on rates of memory loss for dynamical systems with infinite invariant measure exist, with a single exception of a recent paper by I.Chevyrev and A.K. on null recurrent Markov chains.

AI.tldr: Highly accurate numerical estimates of invariant measure properties for Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti intermittent maps, using an Abel function with asymptotic expansion, covering finite and sigma-finite cases.
AI.motivation: A driving motivation is the upcoming proof of optimal memory loss rates valid for both finite and infinite invariant measures. No prior memory-loss results exist for infinite-measure systems except a recent paper on null recurrent Markov chains.
AI.method: Use an Abel function that solves the neutral dynamics, computed accurately via an asymptotic expansion, to overcome non-uniform expansion where the transfer operator lacks a spectral gap.
AI.result: Obtains first practical estimates for parameters far from zero, including the sigma-finite invariant measure case.
AI.conclusion: Enables much deeper numerical study of intermittent dynamics than previously possible.

title: The focusing Calogero--Moser derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation in the Hardy--Zhidkov space: explicit flow formula and dark multi-solitons
summary:
This paper studies the focusing Calogero--Moser derivative nonlinear Schrödinger (CMdNLS) equation under the nonzero boundary condition \(|u(t,x)|\to 1\) as \(|x|\to+\infty\). In sharp contrast to the classical paradigm for the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation, namely that focusing nonlinearities support only bright solitons on a zero background, we show that the focusing CMdNLS equation admits a rich family of \emph{dark multi-soliton} solutions on a nonzero background, whose existence is driven by a spectral gap \([-1,0]\) in the point spectrum of the Lax operator, together with the Hardy space structure.
  The main results are threefold. First, we establish an explicit formula for general solutions in the Hardy--Zhidkov space \(\mathcal Z^2_+\), via a \emph{semigroup method} based on new commutator estimates between the Lax--Beurling shift semigroup and Toeplitz operators. This approach circumvents the non-commutativity of the unbounded generator with the time derivative and requires no weighted hypothesis on solutions or on the domain of validity of commutator formulas. Second, the algebraic definition of dark multi-soliton potentials is shown to be equivalent to two spectral conditions on the Lax operator. Together with the conservation of a generating functional, this yields the invariance of the dark \(N\)-soliton set \(\mathcal U_N\) under the CMdNLS flow. Third, the action-angle variables on \(\mathcal U_N\) are constructed, which establishes the complete integrability of the focusing CMdNLS equation on \(\mathcal U_N\).
  Combining these results, we obtain an inverse spectral formula, from which it follows that the poles of dark multi-soliton solutions satisfy a complexified Calogero--Moser system. Long time asymptotics and uniform Sobolev estimates are also derived.

AI.tldr: The focusing CMdNLS equation with nonzero boundary conditions admits rich dark multi-soliton solutions, driven by a spectral gap, and is completely integrable on the dark N-soliton set.
AI.motivation: Contrasts with the classical cubic NLS paradigm where focusing nonlinearities only support bright solitons on zero background; aims to establish existence and structure of dark multi-solitons on nonzero background.
AI.method: Semigroup method based on new commutator estimates between the Lax–Beurling shift semigroup and Toeplitz operators; spectral conditions on the Lax operator; generating functional conservation; action-angle variables.
AI.result: Explicit solution formula in Hardy–Zhidkov space; algebraic definition of dark multi-soliton potentials equivalent to spectral conditions; invariance of dark N-soliton set under flow; complete integrability via action-angle variables; inverse spectral formula; poles satisfy a complexified Calogero–Moser system; long-time asymptotics and Sobolev estimates.
AI.conclusion: The focusing CMdNLS equation on nonzero background supports dark multi-solitons and is completely integrable on the dark N-soliton set, with the pole dynamics governed by a complexified Calogero–Moser system.

title: Emergence of cuspons through wave breaking
summary: We study the emergence of cuspons through wave breaking, with the Camassa--Holm equation as a principal model. For a broad open class of smooth initial data, the first singularity occurs at a unique point and has the sharp local Hölder regularity \(C^{3/5}\). We construct a continuation of the Lagrangian flow through this singular time and reconstruct from it a conservative Eulerian weak solution. We show that the first singularity does not simply persist after breaking; instead, it bifurcates immediately into an anticuspon--cuspon pair, each having the sharp local Hölder regularity \(C^{2/3}\), with opposite one-sided slope orientations. The two singular branches move apart from the original breaking point, and the portion of the profile between them reverses its local monotonicity. The proof is based on an extended inverse-slope variable that remains regular through wave breaking. At the first singular time, this variable has a nondegenerate quadratic zero, which splits immediately afterward into two simple zeros. The corresponding degeneracy of the Lagrangian flow map converts the quadratic first-breaking geometry into the \(C^{3/5}\) profile and the post-breaking simple-zero geometry into the \(C^{2/3}\) cuspon profiles. The generalized Hunter--Saxton family provides an explicit realization of the same Lagrangian mechanism and also allows us to track the subsequent interaction and annihilation of the singular branches. Thus an anticuspon--cuspon pair emerges dynamically from smooth initial data through wave breaking, rather than being imposed through a singular traveling-wave ansatz.

AI.tldr: Cuspons emerge dynamically from smooth data via wave breaking in the Camassa–Holm equation: the first singularity at a unique point with C^{3/5} regularity bifurcates immediately into an anticuspon–cuspon pair with C^{2/3} regularity, proven via an extended inverse-slope variable.
AI.motivation: Cuspons are typically imposed through a singular traveling-wave ansatz rather than arising from smooth initial data. This work aims to show that they emerge dynamically through wave breaking, providing a rigorous description of the singularity's formation and immediate splitting.
AI.method: An extended inverse-slope variable is used, which stays regular through wave breaking. It has a nondegenerate quadratic zero at the first singular time that splits into two simple zeros. The corresponding degeneracy of the Lagrangian flow map converts the quadratic first-breaking geometry into the C^{3/5} profile, and the post-breaking simple-zero geometry into C^{2/3} cuspon profiles. A continuation of the Lagrangian flow is constructed and used to rebuild a conservative Eulerian weak solution; the generalized Hunter–Saxton family provides an explicit realization.
AI.result: For a broad open class of smooth initial data, the first singularity occurs at a unique point with sharp local Hölder regularity C^{3/5}. After breaking, it bifurcates immediately into an anticuspon–cuspon pair, each with sharp local Hölder regularity C^{2/3} and opposite one-sided slope orientations. The two singular branches move apart, and the profile between them reverses its local monotonicity.
AI.conclusion: An anticuspon–cuspon pair emerges dynamically from smooth initial data through wave breaking rather than being imposed via a singular traveling-wave ansatz. The generalized Hunter–Saxton family also allows tracking of the subsequent interaction and annihilation of the singular branches.

title: Instantaneous Exponential Ill-posedness of the BGK Model in a Half-Space with Inflow Boundary Conditions
summary: In this paper, we study boundary-driven behavior of the BGK model and the Boltzmann equation in a half-space with vacuum initial data. For any $1\leqβ\leq2$ and $α>0$, we construct a unique local-in-time BGK solution whose inflow boundary data have an arbitrarily small norm with the tangential exponential weight $e^{α|v_h|^β}$, but whose norm with weight $e^{α'|v_h|^β}$ is infinite for every $0<α'\leqα$ and every positive time of existence, where $v=(v_h,v_z)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $v_h\in\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$ denotes the tangential velocity. Thus, this BGK solution instantaneously leaves the exponentially weighted spaces associated with the inflow data, even when the exponential weight is weakened. The construction relies on sharp estimates for the density, bulk velocity, and temperature on a singular scale together with a fixed-point argument in a time-dependent anisotropic space. For comparison, we establish local existence and uniqueness for the cutoff Boltzmann equation under isotropic exponential weights $e^{α|v|^β}$. In the Appendix, we further clarify the role of these different weights by showing that the macroscopic stability required for the BGK construction can fail even for Maxwellian inflow data and that it can be recovered by suitably weakening the normal velocity decay of the inflow data. These observations highlight a structural difference between local Maxwellian relaxation and the Boltzmann collision operator in the presence of boundary inflow and vacuum initial data. This work extends the whole-space analysis of D. Lee, S. Park, and S.-B. Yun \cite{LPY2024} to the half-space setting.

AI.tldr: The paper studies boundary-driven BGK and Boltzmann equations in a half-space with vacuum initial data, showing a BGK solution that instantaneously exits even weakened exponential weighted spaces, revealing a structural difference from the Boltzmann operator.
AI.motivation: To extend the whole-space analysis of Lee-Park-Yun to the half-space setting and to understand how boundary inflow, vacuum initial data, and exponential velocity weights interact for the BGK model versus the Boltzmann equation.
AI.method: Constructs a unique local-in-time BGK solution via sharp estimates for density, bulk velocity, and temperature on a singular scale, combined with a fixed-point argument in a time-dependent anisotropic space. For comparison, establishes local existence and uniqueness for the cutoff Boltzmann equation under isotropic exponential weights.
AI.result: For any 1≤β≤2 and α>0, there is a BGK solution with arbitrarily small tangential exponential inflow data norm e^{α|v_h|^β}, yet infinite norm under weight e^{α'|v_h|^β} for all 0<α'≤α at any positive time. Local existence and uniqueness hold for the cutoff Boltzmann equation under isotropic weights. Appendix shows macroscopic stability for BGK can fail even for Maxwellian inflow and can be recovered by weakening normal velocity decay.
AI.conclusion: The BGK solution instantaneously leaves exponentially weighted spaces associated with inflow data, even when the weight is weakened, whereas the Boltzmann equation behaves differently—highlighting a structural difference between local Maxwellian relaxation and the Boltzmann collision operator under boundary inflow with vacuum initial data.

title: Global classical solutions for a metastatic cancer invasion model with negative haptotaxis
summary: We analyze a coupled PDE-ODE model for metastatic cancer invasion involving epithelial-like and mesenchymal-like cancer cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), the transforming growth factor $β$, matrix-degrading metalloproteinases, and extracellular matrix reconstruction by CAFs. The model incorporates bidirectional phenotypic transitions between epithelial-like and mesenchymal-like cancer cells, cancer-cell haptotaxis, negative fibroblast haptotaxis, as well as cell-specific proliferation. Under explicit parameter restrictions, we establish global classical solvability for the full model in two dimensions using an energy-based approach, and for a three-dimensional variant with constant phenotypic transition rates using coupled $L^p$-estimates. Numerical simulations illustrate primary tumor invasion and metastatic spread to secondary sites.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a coupled PDE-ODE model of metastatic cancer invasion (epithelial/mesenchymal cancer cells, CAFs, TGF-β, MMPs, ECM remodeling) and establishes global classical solvability in 2D and a 3D variant, with numerical simulations of invasion and metastasis.
AI.motivation: Metastatic invasion involves complex interactions among cancer cell phenotypes, CAFs, signaling factors, and ECM remodeling; a rigorous mathematical understanding of such coupled dynamics and their well-posedness is needed.
AI.method: A coupled PDE-ODE system incorporating bidirectional epithelial-mesenchymal phenotypic transitions, cancer-cell haptotaxis, negative fibroblast haptotaxis, cell-specific proliferation, TGF-β and MMP dynamics, and CAF-mediated ECM reconstruction. Global classical solvability is proved via an energy-based approach in 2D and via coupled L^p-estimates for a 3D variant with constant transition rates.
AI.result: Under explicit parameter restrictions, global classical solutions are established for the full model in two dimensions, and for the three-dimensional variant with constant phenotypic transition rates. Numerical simulations reproduce primary tumor invasion and metastatic spread to secondary sites.
AI.conclusion: The model is globally well-posed under suitable conditions in 2D (and a 3D variant), providing a rigorous foundation and simulation framework for studying metastatic cancer invasion.

title: The anisotropic Calderón problem for Riemannian metrics at high fixed frequency
summary: We study an inverse boundary value problem for the Helmholtz equation on a smooth compact non-trapping Riemannian manifold with strictly convex boundary. We prove that, given two such metrics, for sufficiently large but fixed frequency $λ$, equality of their Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps implies equality of their lens data, up to a smooth boundary-fixing diffeomorphism. This establishes a high-frequency bridge between the Calderón problem and lens rigidity. We also prove a quantitative version of this result uniformly valid in a suitable bounded set of Riemannian metrics. Crucially, we show that Gaussian beam type solutions concentrating on maximal geodesics, split near the boundary into outgoing/incoming parts, such that the phase of the outgoing part contains information on exit point, direction, and travel time. The recovery of lens data then proceeds by a careful stationary phase analysis and a boundary integral identity.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that for a fixed large frequency, equality of Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps for the Helmholtz equation on non-trapping Riemannian manifolds with strictly convex boundary implies equality of lens data up to a boundary-fixing diffeomorphism, linking the Calderón problem to lens rigidity.
AI.motivation: The paper seeks to connect two central inverse problems—the Calderón problem (recovering a metric from boundary measurements) and lens rigidity (recovering a metric from scattering/lens data)—in the high-frequency regime.
AI.method: Gaussian beam-type solutions concentrating on maximal geodesics are constructed; these split near the boundary into outgoing/incoming parts whose phase encodes exit point, direction, and travel time. Lens data recovery follows via stationary phase analysis and a boundary integral identity.
AI.result: For sufficiently large but fixed frequency, equality of Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps implies equality of lens data up to a smooth boundary-fixing diffeomorphism. A quantitative version holds uniformly on a bounded set of Riemannian metrics.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a high-frequency bridge between the Calderón problem and lens rigidity, with quantitative stability, via Gaussian beam constructions and stationary phase arguments.

title: The Allen-Cahn equation and general minimal cones
summary: We construct solutions to the Allen-Cahn equation $Δu+u-u^3=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^{N+1}$, with $N\ge 3$, whose zero level set is asymptotic (at infinity) to a given minimal cone. Our construction is quite general, since we only use a suitable nondegeneracy assumption; neither stability nor symmetry of the underlying cone is required. Moreover, we calculate the morse index of such solutions. In particular, our main result generalizes a result by Pacard and Wei (2013) dealing with stable solutions to the Allen-Cahn equation in high dimensions. More precisely, we give a positive answer to a remark raised in the paper by Pacard and Wei about the possibility to relax the assumption for the underlying cone is area-minimizing or at least stable. As a corollary, we also obtain solutions with infinite morse index and connected zero level set.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs solutions to the Allen-Cahn equation in R^{N+1} (N≥3) whose zero level set is asymptotic to a given minimal cone, requiring only a nondegeneracy assumption, and computes their Morse index.
AI.motivation: Previous work by Pacard and Wei (2013) treated stable solutions to the Allen-Cahn equation in high dimensions, but asked whether the stability or area-minimizing assumption on the underlying cone could be relaxed. This paper addresses that open remark.
AI.method: The authors build solutions whose zero level set asymptotically approaches a prescribed minimal cone, using only a suitable nondegeneracy assumption—no stability or symmetry of the cone is needed. They also compute the Morse index of the constructed solutions.
AI.result: The construction works for general minimal cones (N≥3) without stability, symmetry, or area-minimizing requirements. The Morse index of the solutions is calculated, and as a corollary, solutions with infinite Morse index and connected zero level set are obtained.
AI.conclusion: The main result generalizes Pacard and Wei's result, positively answering their remark about relaxing the assumption that the underlying cone be area-minimizing or stable, and yields new solutions with infinite Morse index and connected zero level set.

title: The Asymptotic Theory of Ginzburg--Landau Critical Points on Domains with Corners
summary: We study the critical points $U_\varepsilon$ of the two-dimensional Ginzburg--Landau energy on domains with corners $Ω$ and imposed Dirichlet boundary condition which vanishes precisely at the vertices $V$. We isolate the forced scalar boundary layer $ρ_\varepsilon$ by the weighted Lassoued--Mironescu splitting. Assuming the reduced logarithmic energy bound and vertex logarithmic tightness, we prove that after passing to a subsequence, the normalized maps $v_\varepsilon = U_\varepsilon/ρ_\varepsilon$ converges in $C^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(Ω\setminus A)$ $\forall k\ge0$ away from a finite set of interior vortices $A$. The limiting map is a canonical $S^1$-valued harmonic map $u_*$ containing integer interior vortex factors and fixed fractional corner factors. The renormalized energy is defined by removing discs around the interior vortices and sectors around the vertices and subtracting the corresponding logarithmic divergences. The interior vortex locations of the limiting map are critical points of this renormalized energy.

AI.tldr: Analysis of critical points of 2D Ginzburg-Landau energy on cornered domains with vanishing Dirichlet data at vertices; the normalized maps converge to a canonical S^1-valued harmonic map with interior vortices and corner factors, whose locations are critical points of a renormalized energy.
AI.motivation: Vortices and boundary layers in Ginzburg-Landau theory are well studied on smooth domains, but domains with corners and vanishing boundary conditions at vertices introduce fractional corner factors and forced scalar boundary layers that require careful asymptotic analysis.
AI.method: Isolate the forced scalar boundary layer via the weighted Lassoued-Mironescu splitting; assume a reduced logarithmic energy bound and vertex logarithmic tightness; pass to a subsequence and study convergence of normalized maps v_ε = U_ε/ρ_ε in C^k_loc away from a finite interior vortex set A; define a renormalized energy by excising discs around interior vortices and sectors around vertices and subtracting logarithmic divergences.
AI.result: The normalized maps converge in C^k_loc(Ω\A) for all k≥0 to a canonical S^1-valued harmonic map u_* containing integer interior vortex factors and fixed fractional corner factors; the interior vortex locations are critical points of the renormalized energy.
AI.conclusion: Provides a compactness and limiting description for Ginzburg-Landau critical points on cornered domains, characterizing the limit as a harmonic map whose vortex positions minimize (are critical points of) the renormalized energy.

title: The Vanishing-Diffusion Limit of an Incompressible Visco-Morphoelastic System: Weak Solutions and a Jaumann Defect
summary: We study an incompressible visco-morphoelastic system in three dimensions in which the Eulerian effective strain is transported by the Zaremba-Jaumann rate and coupled to a Navier-Stokes momentum balance through a Kelvin-Voigt stress. The strain remains symmetric and splits into a scalar transport-relaxation equation for its trace and a deviatoric equation containing the nonlinear stretching and Jaumann terms. We regularize both equations by diffusion of order $\varepsilon$, which admits a mechanical interpretation as weakly nonlocal remodeling with a characteristic length scale. For fixed $\varepsilon>0$ we construct Leray-Hopf type weak solutions by a truncated Galerkin scheme and remove the truncation a posteriori using a maximum principle for the scalar variable. As $\varepsilon\to0$, the scalar variable converges strongly in $L^p((0,T)\timesΩ)$ for every $1\le p<\infty$, by a DiPerna-Lions commutator argument on bounded Lipschitz domains, allowing the stretching term to be identified in the limit. In contrast, the Jaumann commutator is a product of two weakly convergent sequences, and its limit cannot be identified from the available estimates. We therefore obtain a defect \[\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}\in L^2(0,T;(H^2(Ω;\mathbb{S}_0))^\ast)\] in the limiting deviatoric equation. We give two sufficient conditions for $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}=0$. The energy-level cancellation used in related corotational viscoelastic models does not close here because the coefficient of the stretching term is itself an unknown.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs Leray-Hopf weak solutions for a 3D incompressible visco-morphoelastic system with Zaremba-Jaumann transported strain and Kelvin-Voigt stress, regularized by ε-order diffusion, and analyzes the ε→0 limit, obtaining strong convergence for the scalar trace but an unidentifiable defect in the deviatoric equation.
AI.motivation: Understanding the vanishing-diffusion limit of a visco-morphoelastic system where the Eulerian effective strain is transported by the Zaremba-Jaumann rate and coupled to Navier-Stokes via Kelvin-Voigt stress, and determining whether the limiting deviatoric equation closes.
AI.method: Regularize both the scalar transport-relaxation and deviatoric strain equations by ε-order diffusion (weakly nonlocal remodeling with a length scale). Construct Leray-Hopf weak solutions via a truncated Galerkin scheme for fixed ε>0, removing the truncation using a maximum principle. Take ε→0 using a DiPerna-Lions commutator argument on bounded Lipschitz domains; compare with the Jaumann commutator product of two weakly convergent sequences.
AI.result: For fixed ε>0, Leray-Hopf weak solutions exist. As ε→0, the scalar variable converges strongly in L^p((0,T)×Ω) for all 1≤p<∞, letting the stretching term be identified. The Jaumann commutator cannot be identified, yielding a defect D in L^2(0,T;(H^2(Ω;S_0))*) in the limiting deviatoric equation. Two sufficient conditions for D=0 are given. The energy-level cancellation used in related corotational viscoelastic models does not close because the stretching coefficient is unknown.
AI.conclusion: The vanishing-diffusion limit of the visco-morphoelastic system is only partially closed: the scalar part passes to the limit strongly, but the deviatoric equation retains a defect that vanishes under two sufficient conditions, and standard corotational cancellation fails due to the unknown stretching coefficient.

title: Determining $W^{1,n}$ conductivities in Calderón's problem for $n\geq4$
summary: We establish a global uniqueness result at the critical Sobolev regularity for the isotropic Calderón problem in all dimensions $n\ge 4$. More precisely, for every $n\ge4$ and every bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, any real-valued, uniformly elliptic scalar conductivity $γ\in W^{1,n}(Ω)$ is uniquely determined by its full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. This settles a long-standing open problem in the field. To prove uniqueness at this endpoint, we develop an averaged trace norm method, which combines complex geometrical optics with trace norm estimates averaged over wave orientations.

AI.tldr: The paper proves global uniqueness for the isotropic Calderón problem at the critical Sobolev regularity in all dimensions n≥4, showing that any W^{1,n} scalar conductivity on a bounded Lipschitz domain is uniquely determined by its Dirichlet-to-Neumann map.
AI.motivation: The Calderón problem at the critical Sobolev regularity (W^{1,n}) remained a long-standing open problem. Prior results did not establish uniqueness at this endpoint regularity, and the challenge lies in handling conductivities at the precise threshold where standard methods fail.
AI.method: The authors develop an averaged trace norm method, which combines complex geometrical optics (CGO) with trace norm estimates averaged over wave orientations, to prove uniqueness at the endpoint regularity.
AI.result: For every n≥4 and every bounded Lipschitz domain Ω⊂R^n, any real-valued, uniformly elliptic scalar conductivity γ∈W^{1,n}(Ω) is uniquely determined by its full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map.
AI.conclusion: The work settles a long-standing open problem by establishing global uniqueness for the isotropic Calderón problem at critical Sobolev regularity in all dimensions n≥4.

title: Sharp higher-order uncertainty principles
summary: We establish a class of sharp higher-order inequalities related to the uncertainty principle. First, by means of the expanding the squares method, we give a concise proof of sharp higher-order Heisenberg uncertainty principles. We provide explicit expressions for the optimal constants and establish the existence of extremal functions. Furthermore, we obtain sharp higher-order Heisenberg uncertainty principles for curl-free vector fields. In particular, when $N=2$, we give an answer to the higher-order version of Open Problem 9 raised by Maz'ya in [Integr. Equ. Oper. Theory (2018) 90:25]. Second, we establish sharp higher-order Heisenberg uncertainty principles that do not involve higher-order tensors. We also prove sharp higher-order Heisenberg uncertainty principles and higher-order hydrogen uncertainty principles for radially symmetric functions.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a class of sharp higher-order inequalities related to the uncertainty principle, providing optimal constants, extremal functions, and answers a higher-order version of Maz'ya's Open Problem 9 for N=2.
AI.motivation: To extend the classical Heisenberg uncertainty principle to higher orders with sharp constants and extend to curl-free vector fields and radially symmetric functions, addressing open problems in the field.
AI.method: The authors use the expanding the squares method to give concise proofs of sharp higher-order Heisenberg uncertainty principles, deriving explicit optimal constants and establishing existence of extremal functions.
AI.result: Sharp higher-order Heisenberg uncertainty principles are obtained with explicit optimal constants and existence of extremal functions; also derived for curl-free vector fields, answering the higher-order version of Maz'ya's Open Problem 9 (N=2). Additional results include versions without higher-order tensors and principles for radially symmetric functions including higher-order hydrogen uncertainty principles.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a unified and sharp treatment of higher-order uncertainty principles, resolving an open problem and extending results to structured settings.

title: Semigroup Criteria for Blow-up and Global Existence of Semilinear Heat Equations on Metric Measure Spaces
summary: We study finite-time blow-up and global existence for semilinear heat equations with time-dependent reaction coefficients on metric measure spaces. For convex nonlinearities, we establish a blow-up criterion that retains the dependence on the initial datum through its linear evolution and does not require stochastic completeness. Under additional conservativity and heat kernel assumptions, we also prove blow-up at the critical Fujita exponent associated with polynomial volume growth. Our main global existence result is based on a heat-kernel-weighted functional space in which the mild solution map becomes a contraction. This yields a unified construction covering both polynomial and exponential heat kernel decay, general locally Lipschitz nonlinearities, and time-dependent reaction coefficients, without convexity or monotonicity assumptions. In particular, the global existence criterion only uses the behaviour of the nonlinearity on the range explored by the solution. Applications include Riemannian manifolds, metric graphs, and, within a separate discrete framework, weighted graphs. The arguments, especially the functional construction underlying global existence, are new and lead to new results even for the classical underlying spaces considered above.

AI.tldr: The paper studies finite-time blow-up and global existence for semilinear heat equations with time-dependent reaction coefficients on metric measure spaces, establishing a blow-up criterion for convex nonlinearities and a unified global existence construction via a heat-kernel-weighted functional space.
AI.motivation: Extends semilinear heat equation theory beyond classical Euclidean settings to general metric measure spaces, addressing limitations of prior results that often require stochastic completeness, convexity, or monotonicity assumptions.
AI.method: For convex nonlinearities, derives a blow-up criterion depending on the initial datum via its linear evolution without requiring stochastic completeness; under conservativity and heat kernel assumptions, proves blow-up at the critical Fujita exponent linked to polynomial volume growth; constructs a heat-kernel-weighted functional space where the mild solution map is a contraction, yielding unified global existence results for polynomial and exponential heat kernel decay, general locally Lipschitz nonlinearities, and time-dependent coefficients.
AI.result: Obtains a blow-up criterion retaining initial-datum dependence, blow-up at the critical Fujita exponent under additional assumptions, and a unified global existence criterion depending only on the nonlinearity over the solution's explored range, without convexity or monotonicity; applies to Riemannian manifolds, metric graphs, and weighted graphs.
AI.conclusion: The functional-space construction and arguments are novel, yielding new results even for classical underlying spaces and providing a unified framework for blow-up and global existence on diverse metric measure spaces.

title: Vanishing orders of Dirichlet solutions to the Schrödinger equation in dimensions three and higher
summary: Let $B_3=B(0,3)\subset\mathbb{R}^3$. For every sufficiently large integer $k$, we construct a nonzero real function $u_k\in C^2(\overline{B_3})$ and a real potential $V_k\in L^\infty(B_3)$ such that $Δu_k=V_ku_k$, $u_k|_{\partial B_3}=0$, $\mathrm{ord}_0u_k=k$, and $\|V_k\|_\infty\le Ck^{3/2}$. Consequently, for every sufficiently large $N$, there is such a Dirichlet solution with potential norm smaller than $N$ and vanishing order at least $cN^{2/3}$. The construction extends directly to higher dimensions and to spheres. Together with previous results, this example indicates that $C(1+\|V\|_\infty^{2/3})$ is the sharp bound for the vanishing order in the real-valued case. It also indicates that the bound conjectured independently by Kukavica \cite{Kukavica1998} and Kenig \cite{Kenig2006} is not attainable in general.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs, for each large k, a nonzero Dirichlet eigenfunction of Δu=Vu on B_3 with vanishing order k at the origin and bounded potential, showing the sharp vanishing-order bound is C(1+‖V‖∞^{2/3}) and disproving a conjectured bound by Kukavica and Kenig.
AI.motivation: Understanding how large the vanishing order of a solution to Δu=Vu can be in terms of the potential's size is a central quantitative unique continuation question. Prior bounds existed, and Kukavica (1998) and Kenig (2006) independently conjectured a stronger bound; whether it holds was open.
AI.method: They explicitly build, for every sufficiently large integer k, a nonzero real C² function u_k vanishing on ∂B_3 and a real L^∞ potential V_k with Δu_k=V_ku_k, ord_0 u_k=k, and ‖V_k‖∞≤Ck^{3/2}. The construction directly generalizes to higher dimensions and to spheres.
AI.result: For all large N there is a Dirichlet solution with potential norm below N and vanishing order at least cN^{2/3}. Combined with earlier results, this shows C(1+‖V‖∞^{2/3}) is the sharp bound on vanishing order in the real-valued case.
AI.conclusion: The sharp vanishing-order bound is C(1+‖V‖∞^{2/3}); the bound conjectured independently by Kukavica and Kenig is not attainable in general.

title: On regularity of averaged Green's functions in homogenization of elliptic PDE
summary: This paper is concerned with establishing estimates on averaged Green's functions for a uniformly elliptic divergence form partial difference equation with random coefficients on the $d$ dimensional integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$. It has previously been shown that the averaged Green's function is point-wise well approximated by the homogenized Green's function at large length scales. Corresponding results also hold for (fractional) derivatives of the averaged Green's function up to but not including the second derivative. Second derivative results have been established when the elliptic equation generates a positive semi-group, as in the diagonal case. Here the second derivative result is shown more generally by using an insight of Bourgain.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes estimates on averaged Green's functions for uniformly elliptic divergence-form random-coefficient difference equations on Z^d, extending second-derivative results to the general (non-diagonal) case via an insight of Bourgain.
AI.motivation: Prior work showed averaged Green's functions are well approximated by homogenized ones at large scales, including fractional derivatives up to but not including the second derivative. Second-derivative results existed only when the equation generates a positive semi-group (diagonal case). This paper removes that restriction.
AI.method: Uses an insight of Bourgain to establish second-derivative estimates for the averaged Green's function generally, without requiring the positive semi-group condition.
AI.result: Second-derivative estimates on averaged Green's functions are shown to hold in the general uniformly elliptic divergence-form setting, generalizing beyond the diagonal case.
AI.conclusion: Bourgain's insight allows extension of the second-derivative homogenization results to general uniformly elliptic random difference equations.

title: Local separation profiles for the stationary Prandtl system
summary:
We construct solutions to the two-dimensional stationary Prandtl system under a constant adverse pressure gradient exhibiting a family of distinct separation laws. More precisely, for every integer $\ell\ge1$, we construct smooth initial data for which separation occurs at a finite location $x=x^\ast$, with \[ \partial_y u(x,0) =\mathbf C_\ell(x^\ast-x)^{\ell/2}\bigl(1+o(1)\bigr), \qquad x\uparrow x^\ast, \] where $\mathbf C_\ell>0$ depends on the initial data.
  We determine the local asymptotic structure of the solution near separation through matched inner and outer expansions based on linearization around the ground state in von Mises variables. This description addresses Open Problem~5 posed by Oleinik and Samokhin~\cite{OleinikSamok-book-99}. We also prove that the square-root separation regime, corresponding to $\ell=1$, is dynamically stable under small admissible perturbations of the initial data in a suitable topology.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs solutions to the 2D stationary Prandtl system with constant adverse pressure gradient, exhibiting a whole family of distinct separation laws indexed by an integer l>=1, and resolves Open Problem 5 of Oleinik and Samokhin.
AI.motivation: Classical Prandtl separation theory typically predicts a single (square-root) separation law. Understanding whether other separation laws exist, and characterizing them, was left open by Oleinik and Samokhin (Open Problem 5). The paper aims to fill this gap by constructing a full family of separation behaviors and analyzing their local structure and stability.
AI.method: Matched inner and outer asymptotic expansions for the stationary Prandtl system with constant adverse pressure gradient, based on linearization around the ground state in von Mises variables. Smooth initial data are constructed so that separation occurs at a finite point x=x*, with ∂_y u(x,0) ~ C_l (x*-x)^{l/2}. A dynamic stability analysis is performed for the square-root regime (l=1) under small admissible perturbations in a suitable topology.
AI.result: For every integer l>=1, smooth initial data are constructed for which separation occurs at a finite location x=x*, with ∂_y u(x,0) = C_l (x*-x)^{l/2}(1+o(1)) as x↑x*, where C_l>0 depends on the initial data. The local asymptotic structure near separation is determined via matched inner/outer expansions. The square-root separation regime (l=1) is shown to be dynamically stable under small admissible perturbations of the initial data in a suitable topology.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a family of distinct separation laws for the 2D stationary Prandtl system, provides their local asymptotic description, resolves Open Problem 5 of Oleinik and Samokhin, and proves dynamical stability of the square-root separation regime.

title: Nonlinear stability of the Guderley imploding shock wave in radial symmetry
summary: We prove nonlinear stability of the Guderley imploding shock under radial perturbations for the three-dimensional compressible Euler equations in the adiabatic range $1<γ\leq\frac{5}{3}$. The perturbed solutions develop an asymptotically self-similar implosion in finite time. Our result allows perturbations with small, nonzero constant pressure in the quiescent region ahead of the shock. The proof combines weighted $L^\infty$ estimates along characteristics with a computer-assisted proof of stability inequalities for the Guderley profile.

AI.tldr: Nonlinear stability of the Guderley imploding shock under radial perturbations is proven for 3D compressible Euler equations in the adiabatic range 1 < γ ≤ 5/3, with asymptotically self-similar finite-time implosion.
AI.motivation: Understanding stability of self-similar imploding shocks like Guderley's is important for modeling finite-time singularity formation (implosion) in compressible fluids, and prior works left nonlinear stability and nonzero background pressure open.
AI.method: Combines weighted L-infinity estimates along characteristics with a computer-assisted proof of stability inequalities for the Guderley profile.
AI.result: Perturbed solutions develop an asymptotically self-similar implosion in finite time; the result holds for $1<γ≤5/3$ and permits small nonzero constant pressure ahead of the shock.
AI.conclusion: The Guderley imploding shock is nonlinearly stable under radial perturbations, extending validity to nonzero pressure in the quiescent region.

title: Regularity for solutions to inhomogeneous degenerate parabolic $p$-Laplace equations
summary: For weak solutions to quasilinear degenerate parabolic equations of $p$-Laplace type, a central obstacle in applying the method of intrinsic scaling to prove their Hölder regularity is the derivation of forward-in-time propagation estimate for the spatial measure of level sets. In this paper, we revisit and overcome this difficulty for an inhomogeneous degenerate parabolic $p$-Laplace equation with bounded nonnegative time-independent forcing term and initial data. Our new proof is built upon the temporal Lipschitz estimate that we establish on any time interval separated from the initial time by a positive amount. The strong regularity gain furnished by this estimate allows us to derive the forward propagation of level-set measures directly, thereby bypassing the energy inequality that served as the starting point of the previous approach. Furthermore, we establish space-time $W^{1,\infty}_{x,t}$ estimates away from the initial time and construct counterexamples to demonstrate the sharpness of the positive waiting-time condition under merely bounded initial data.

AI.tldr: The paper revisits Hölder regularity for inhomogeneous degenerate parabolic p-Laplace equations by establishing a temporal Lipschitz estimate to bypass energy inequalities, deriving forward propagation of level-set measures, proving space-time W^{1,∞}_{x,t} estimates, and constructing counterexamples showing sharpness of the positive waiting-time condition under bounded initial data.
AI.motivation: Applying the method of intrinsic scaling to prove Hölder regularity for weak solutions of quasilinear degenerate parabolic equations of p-Laplace type faces a central obstacle: deriving a forward-in-time propagation estimate for the spatial measure of level sets. This work aims to overcome this difficulty for an inhomogeneous degenerate parabolic p-Laplace equation with bounded nonnegative time-independent forcing and initial data.
AI.method: The authors establish a temporal Lipschitz estimate on any time interval separated from the initial time by a positive amount. This strong regularity gain enables the direct derivation of forward propagation of level-set measures, bypassing the energy inequality that served as the starting point of the previous approach. They also establish space-time W^{1,∞}_{x,t} estimates away from the initial time.
AI.result: The forward-in-time propagation estimate for the spatial measure of level sets is derived using the new temporal Lipschitz estimate. Space-time W^{1,∞}_{x,t} estimates away from the initial time are established. Counterexamples demonstrate the sharpness of the positive waiting-time condition under merely bounded initial data.
AI.conclusion: The paper successfully overcomes the central obstacle in intrinsic scaling for Hölder regularity by providing a new route via temporal Lipschitz estimates. The counterexamples confirm that the positive waiting-time condition is sharp when initial data is only bounded.

title: Inverse Energy Cascade and Non-uniqueness for the Advection-Diffusion Equation
summary: We prove non-uniqueness for the advection-diffusion equation with a drift in a logarithmically near-critical class below $L_t^2L_x^\infty$. The first construction is a diffusion-assisted inverse cascade of scalar energy that diverges as $t \to 0$. The second uses compressed inverse mixing, with diffusion acting perturbatively, and produces a bounded parabolic solution with the energy jump at the initial time. In both constructions the drift and scalar are smooth for positive time. We also consider the drift in $L^{2,\infty}_tL^\infty_x$ and solutions satisfying the energy inequality starting from almost every time. In this setting, we prove uniqueness of solutions with bounded energy, and construct non-unique solution with energy blowing up as time goes to zero.

AI.tldr: The paper proves non-uniqueness for the advection-diffusion equation with a drift in a logarithmically near-critical class just below $L_t^2 L_x^\infty$, via two distinct constructions of non-unique solutions.
AI.motivation: To understand well-posedness thresholds for the advection-diffusion equation, specifically how far below the critical $L_t^2 L_x^\infty$ drift class non-uniqueness persists, and to characterize uniqueness when the drift lies in $L^{2,\infty}_t L^\infty_x$ with solutions obeying the energy inequality.
AI.method: Two constructions: (1) a diffusion-assisted inverse cascade of scalar energy that diverges as $t \to 0$; (2) compressed inverse mixing with diffusion acting perturbatively, yielding a bounded parabolic solution with an energy jump at the initial time. Both drifts and scalars are smooth for positive time. The drift in $L^{2,\infty}_t L^\infty_x$ is also analyzed with solutions satisfying the energy inequality from almost every time.
AI.result: Non-uniqueness is established below $L_t^2 L_x^\infty$ in the near-critical logarithmic class. In the $L^{2,\infty}_t L^\infty_x$ setting, uniqueness of bounded-energy solutions is proved, and a non-unique solution with energy blowing up as $t \to 0$ is constructed.
AI.conclusion: The critical drift class $L_t^2 L_x^\infty$ is essentially sharp for uniqueness; below it (even logarithmically) non-uniqueness holds. When the strong time-integrability is relaxed to $L^{2,\infty}_t L^\infty_x$, uniqueness is recovered only for bounded-energy solutions satisfying the energy inequality almost everywhere in time.

title: On a $2x2$ system of conservation laws with discontinuous flux
summary: We study a one-dimensional $2x2$ system of conservation laws with discontinuous flux. We prove the global existence of weak solutions for initial data with sufficiently small total variation. We construct explicitly the associated Riemann solver and analyze its main properties. Finally, we introduce a Glimm-type numerical scheme tailored to the exact Riemann solver and use it to reproduce the wave patterns obtained analytically.

AI.tldr: Global existence of weak solutions for a 1D 2x2 conservation law system with discontinuous flux, via a Riemann solver and a tailored Glimm-type scheme.
AI.motivation: Systems of conservation laws with discontinuous flux arise in many physical models, but existence theory for such 2x2 systems is challenging and less developed.
AI.method: Construct an explicit Riemann solver and analyze its main properties; prove global existence of weak solutions for initial data with small total variation; design a Glimm-type numerical scheme adapted to the exact Riemann solver.
AI.result: Global existence of weak solutions is established for sufficiently small total variation data; numerical simulations reproduce the analytically obtained wave patterns.
AI.conclusion: The Riemann solver and Glimm-type scheme together provide a consistent analytical and numerical framework for this discontinuous-flux system.

title: Compressible steady water waves
summary: In this paper, we consider the existence of small- and large-amplitude compressible water waves. These are solutions of the two-dimensional free boundary isentropic Euler equations subjected to a constant gravitational force and neglecting the effects of surface tension. We study periodic and solitary waves beneath vacuum as well as front-type solutions of the two-phase problem in a channel. Using local and global bifurcation techniques, we construct large families of these waves beginning at an incompressible solution and treating the Mach number (defined in a suitable sense) as the bifurcation parameter. This gives a rigorous version of the classical Janzen--Rayleigh expansion, but also furnishes solution curves that may limit to transsonic flow.

AI.tldr: The paper proves the existence of small- and large-amplitude compressible water waves (periodic, solitary, and front-type) as solutions to the 2D free-boundary isentropic Euler equations with gravity, using bifurcation theory.
AI.motivation: Classical Janzen--Rayleigh expansion is only formal, so a rigorous construction of compressible water waves—especially large-amplitude ones—was lacking.
AI.method: Local and global bifurcation techniques, starting from an incompressible solution and using the Mach number as the bifurcation parameter.
AI.result: Large families of periodic and solitary waves beneath vacuum, plus front-type solutions of the two-phase channel problem, are constructed; solution curves may limit to transsonic flow.
AI.conclusion: The work gives a rigorous version of the Janzen--Rayleigh expansion and provides solution branches potentially reaching transsonic flow.

title: A Brunn-Minkowski Theory for the Distribution of Random Pairs of Points in Convex Bodies
summary:
Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body, let $X$ and $Y$ be independent uniform points of $K$, and set $R_K=(|K|/ω_n)^{1/n}$. We consider the distribution function \[
  D_K(ρ)=\mathbb P\{|X-Y|/R_K<ρ\}, \] and its homogeneous counterpart \begin{equation*}
  \mathcal J_ρ(K)=\iint_{K\times K}\mathbf{1}_{\{|x-y|<ρR_K\}}dxdy. \end{equation*} Thus $D_K(ρ)$ is the proportion of ordered pairs of points of $K$ whose distance is less than $ρR_K$, or equivalently the radial distribution function of the normalized covariogram of $K$.
  The functional satisfies a Brunn--Minkowski inequality, with equality precisely for homothetic bodies, and its differential gives a first Minkowski inequality. We characterize the Borel measures that occur as Wulff differentials: they are exactly the nonzero finite positive measures with zero centroid which are not concentrated on a great subsphere, and the corresponding body is unique up to translation. We further prove fixed-volume and stationary rigidity of the ball in the subcritical range, together with regularity for the resulting equation. At saturation, the equation is the classical Minkowski equation.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the ordered-pair distance distribution D_K(ρ) of a convex body K and its homogeneous counterpart J_ρ(K), showing a Brunn–Minkowski inequality with equality for homothetic bodies, characterizing Wulff-type differentials as nonzero finite positive zero-centroid measures not on a great subsphere, and proving rigidity of the ball plus regularity results.
AI.motivation: The distance distribution function D_K(ρ) encodes geometric information about a convex body K, but its variational and differential structure (and the possibility of inverting it to recover K) is not well understood. The authors aim to place D_K in the framework of Brunn–Minkowski theory and to characterize which measures can arise as its Wulff-type differentials.
AI.method: Define D_K(ρ)=P(|X−Y|/R_K<ρ) for independent uniform points X,Y in K, with R_K=(|K|/ω_n)^{1/n}, and its homogeneous form J_ρ(K). Derive a Brunn–Minkowski inequality for the functional, obtain a first Minkowski inequality from its differential, characterize admissible Wulff differential measures, and prove uniqueness up to translation along with fixed-volume/stationary rigidity and regularity for the associated equation.
AI.result: The functional satisfies a Brunn–Minkowski inequality with equality exactly for homothetic bodies. Its differential yields a first Minkowski inequality. The Borel measures occurring as Wulff differentials are exactly the nonzero finite positive measures with zero centroid that are not concentrated on a great subsphere, and the corresponding body is unique up to translation. Fixed-volume and stationary rigidity of the ball hold in the subcritical range, with regularity for the resulting equation; at saturation it reduces to the classical Minkowski equation.
AI.conclusion: The distance-distribution functional fits into Brunn–Minkowski theory, admits a clean characterization of its Wulff differentials, and exhibits rigidity and regularity properties that recover the classical Minkowski equation at saturation.

title: Global regularity and sparsity for regularised optimal transport
summary:
We study regularised optimal transport with subquadratic or entropic regularisation. Under $C^{1,α}$-assumptions on the marginals and the domains of their support, we prove global gradient-Lipschitz bounds on the potentials, uniform in the regularisation parameter. Moreover, we show that, up to the boundary, the support of the conditional supports $\text{supp}\,π_\varepsilon(\cdot|x)$ behaves like balls of radius $\varepsilon^\frac 4 {d(p-1)+2}$.
  Our work was carried out concurrently and independently of [9]. We obtain the results of [9,Theorem 1.2] under weaker assumptions and with a different proof.

AI.tldr: The paper proves global gradient-Lipschitz bounds (uniform in the regularisation parameter) for the potentials of regularised optimal transport with subquadratic/entropic regularisation, and characterises the local support of conditional plans near the boundary.
AI.motivation: Regularised optimal transport (entropic or subquadratic) is widely used, but quantitative regularity of the potentials and the geometry of the conditional support are not fully understood, especially with bounds that do not degrade as the regularisation parameter vanishes.
AI.method: Under C^{1,α} assumptions on the marginals and the domains of their support, the authors derive global gradient-Lipschitz bounds on the dual potentials that hold uniformly in the regularisation parameter. They then analyse the conditional support supp π_ε(·|x), showing it behaves, up to the boundary, like balls of radius ε^{4/(d(p-1)+2)}.
AI.result: Global gradient-Lipschitz bounds on the potentials, uniform in the regularisation parameter; the conditional support supp π_ε(·|x) behaves like balls of radius ε^{4/(d(p-1)+2)} up to the boundary. The results of [9, Theorem 1.2] are recovered under weaker assumptions and via a different proof.
AI.conclusion: Regularised optimal transport admits uniform gradient-Lipschitz regularity of potentials and a precise boundary-local geometry of conditional supports. The work, done concurrently and independently of [9], strengthens and reproves prior results under weaker hypotheses.

title: Decoupling and Tail Laws for Small-Order Metric-Valued Nonlocal Energies: A Structural View of the Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova Formula
summary: We develop a measure-theoretic framework for small-order limits of nonlocal energies with metric-valued maps. For globally $L^p$ maps, we consider interaction measures whose marginals have uniformly bounded $L^\infty$ densities $a_α$ and $b_α$. If these densities converge weakly-* to $a_\infty$ and $b_\infty$, the normalized energies converge to the $L^p$ energy weighted by $a_\infty+b_\infty$ if and only if the interaction measures escape every bounded rectangle. For maps that are only locally $L^p$, we introduce target laws describing the distribution of the values sampled at infinity. Convergence of their $p$-distance profiles yields the limiting interaction energy for every $1\leq p<\infty$ and arbitrary Polish targets, with integrated $p$-Wasserstein convergence as a sufficient criterion. The arguments include the endpoint $p=1$ and require no linear structure on the target space. Applications include directional and anisotropic Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova formulas, a Bernoulli-law interpretation of fractional perimeters, and an Abelian principle for heat-semigroup energies.

AI.tldr: A measure-theoretic framework for small-order limits of nonlocal energies with metric-valued maps, covering globally and locally L^p maps, with applications to fractional perimeters and heat-semigroup energies.
AI.motivation: To understand small-order (vanishing-order) limits of nonlocal energies for general metric-valued maps, extending beyond linear/vector settings and addressing the lack of a unified framework for such limits.
AI.method: Introduces interaction measures with marginals having uniformly bounded L^∞ densities; studies convergence under weak-* convergence of densities and escape from bounded rectangles. For locally L^p maps, defines target laws (value distributions at infinity) and uses p-distance profile convergence, with integrated p-Wasserstein convergence as a sufficient criterion; handles p=1 and arbitrary Polish targets without linear structure.
AI.result: For globally L^p maps, normalized energies converge to the L^p energy weighted by a_∞+b_∞ iff interaction measures escape every bounded rectangle. For locally L^p maps, convergence of p-distance profiles yields the limiting interaction energy for all 1≤p<∞ and arbitrary Polish targets.
AI.conclusion: The framework unifies small-order limits of nonlocal energies, requiring no linear structure, and yields applications: directional/anisotropic Maz'ya–Shaposhnikova formulas, a Bernoulli-law interpretation of fractional perimeters, and an Abelian principle for heat-semigroup energies.

title: Global existence, uniform boundedness and asymptotic behavior for Gierer--Meinhardt system with critical exponent $qr=(p-1)(s+1)$
summary:
In this paper, we study the following Gierer--Meinhardt system \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_t=d_1Δu-a_1u+u^p/v^q+δ_1(x),\quad x\in Ω, t>0,\\ v_t=d_2Δv-a_2v+u^r/v^s+δ_2(x), \quad x\in Ω, t>0,\\ \partial_νu=\partial_νv=0,\qquad\qquad \qquad\qquad\quad x\in \partial Ω, t>0,\\ u(x,0)=u_0(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_0(x),\quad x\in Ω, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is a bounded domain, $ν$ is the outer norm vector with respect to the smooth boundary $\partial Ω$, $d_1,d_2, p,q,r>0$, $s>-1$, $p-1<r$, $qr=(p-1)(s+1)$, $δ_1(x)$, $δ_2(x)$, $u_0(x)$ and $v_0(x)$ are continuous functions.
  For every pair $d_1,d_2>0$, we respectively establish the global existence, uniform boundedness and asymptotic behavior for Gierer--Meinhardt system with critical exponent $qr=(p-1)(s+1)$ under certain conditions.

AI.tldr: The paper studies a Gierer–Meinhardt reaction-diffusion system with critical exponent and establishes global existence, uniform boundedness, and asymptotic behavior for all diffusion coefficients.
AI.motivation: The Gierer–Meinhardt system models biological pattern formation, and the critical exponent case qr=(p-1)(s+1) is a delicate borderline where classical methods for global existence and boundedness often fail, motivating its detailed analysis.
AI.method: Analysis of the parabolic Gierer–Meinhardt system with Neumann boundary conditions and continuous source terms δ1, δ2, combining a priori estimates and related techniques under the critical exponent relation qr=(p-1)(s+1), p-1<r, and s>-1.
AI.result: For every pair d1, d2>0, global existence, uniform boundedness, and asymptotic behavior of solutions are established under certain conditions.
AI.conclusion: The system admits globally bounded solutions with characterized long-time behavior in the critical exponent regime, for all positive diffusion coefficients.

title: Regularity for the prescribed vertical mean curvature system in the plane
comment: 19 pages, AI was not used in any part of the manuscript, comments are welcome
summary: We prove everywhere regularity for Lipschitz solutions to the prescribed vertical mean curvature system in the plane, where the codimension is arbitrary and the mean curvature is in $L^r, \, r > 2$. This strengthens and extends our previous result on the Lawson-Osserman conjecture, https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.04997.

AI.tldr: The authors prove everywhere regularity for Lipschitz solutions to the prescribed vertical mean curvature system in the plane, with arbitrary codimension and mean curvature in L^r (r>2), strengthening and extending their prior result on the Lawson-Osserman conjecture.
AI.motivation: Extends prior work on the Lawson-Osserman conjecture by relaxing regularity assumptions and generalizing to arbitrary codimension.
AI.method: Establish everywhere regularity for Lipschitz solutions of the prescribed vertical mean curvature system in the plane.
AI.result: Lipschitz solutions are everywhere regular, with mean curvature in L^r for r>2 and arbitrary codimension.
AI.conclusion: Strengthens and extends the earlier result on the Lawson-Osserman conjecture.

title: Sharp Small-Height Estimates for Subcritical Special Lagrangian Equations in Dimension Three
summary:
We prove an interior Lipschitz estimate with a sharp height threshold for continuous viscosity solutions of the three-dimensional special Lagrangian equation with subcritical phase $|Θ|<π/2$. If \[
  osc_{B_R}u\leq MR^2,\qquad 0\leq M<\secΘ, \] then $Lip_{B_{ρR}}u\leq CR$ for some $ρ>0$ and $C>0$ depending only on $|Θ|$ and $M$. The threshold is optimal: at $M=\secΘ$, there are entire real-analytic solutions whose Lipschitz seminorms are unbounded on every fixed interior ball. The proof uses a two-point maximum principle and algebraic identities specific to dimension three.

AI.tldr: Interior Lipschitz estimate with sharp height threshold for 3D special Lagrangian equation (subcritical phase), proving M < secΘ threshold is optimal.
AI.motivation: To establish an interior Lipschitz estimate with a sharp height threshold for continuous viscosity solutions of the three-dimensional special Lagrangian equation with subcritical phase.
AI.method: Uses a two-point maximum principle and algebraic identities specific to dimension three.
AI.result: If osc_{B_R}u ≤ MR² with 0 ≤ M < secΘ, then Lip_{B_{ρR}}u ≤ CR for some ρ, C. The threshold M = secΘ is optimal, with entire real-analytic solutions having unbounded Lipschitz seminorms on every interior ball.
AI.conclusion: The result gives a sharp height threshold for Lipschitz regularity of the 3D special Lagrangian equation, with optimality demonstrated by explicit counterexamples at M = secΘ.

title: Global Hölder estimates for linearized Monge-Ampère equations in divergence form with applications to dual semigeostrophic equations and periodic homogenization
comment: 30 pages. The argument leading to Proposition 1.2 was first produced in repeated interactions with OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra
summary: We establish interior and global Hölder estimates for linearized Monge-Ampère equations in divergence form in all dimensions $n\geq 3$, when the Hessian determinant of the convex Monge-Ampère potential is bounded above and below by positive constants and the vector field on the right-hand side is bounded. The estimates use the $L^p$ norm of the solution for any $p>1$. A key ingredient is an $L^1$ estimate, with appropriate decay rates, for the gradient of the Green's function of the linearized Monge-Ampère operator in small sections, uniform with respect to the pole. As applications, we obtain uniform Hölder estimates for the time derivatives of the primal and dual potentials in the three-dimensional periodic dual semigeostrophic system when the initial density is bounded away from zero and infinity, and establish a linear convergence rate for periodic homogenization of the Monge-Ampère equation.

AI.tldr: This paper proves interior and global Hölder estimates for linearized Monge-Ampère equations in divergence form for dimensions n≥3, using Green's function gradient L¹ estimates as a key tool.
AI.motivation: Hölder regularity for linearized Monge-Ampère equations in divergence form in higher dimensions was not fully established, and such estimates are needed for applications in semigeostrophic systems and homogenization.
AI.method: Establish interior and global Hölder estimates under bounded Hessian determinant (positive upper/lower bounds) and bounded right-hand vector field; use the L^p norm of the solution (any p>1). Key ingredient: an L¹ estimate with decay rates for the gradient of the Green's function of the linearized Monge-Ampère operator in small sections, uniform in the pole.
AI.result: Obtains Hölder estimates for the linearized Monge-Ampère equation. As applications: uniform Hölder estimates for time derivatives of primal and dual potentials in the 3D periodic dual semigeostrophic system (initial density bounded away from zero and infinity), and a linear convergence rate for periodic homogenization of the Monge-Ampère equation.
AI.conclusion: The Green's function gradient estimate yields robust Hölder regularity, with significant consequences for semigeostrophic dynamics and Monge-Ampère homogenization.

title: Geometry and Convergence of Quadratically Regularized Optimal Transport II
summary: We study quadratically regularized optimal transport with quadratic cost in the regime of small regularization $\varepsilon$, where the support of the optimal coupling is sparse. For smooth marginal densities in $\mathbb{R}^d$, we show that the support contains the graph of the Brenier map. After centering by the Brenier image and rescaling by $\ell=\varepsilon^{1/(d+2)}$, the sections of the support have explicit ellipsoidal limits for $\varepsilon\to0$, except at boundary points, where the limits are half-space profiles. The optimal dual potentials admit expansions at order $\ell^2$, uniformly up to the boundary. We identify the leading coefficients, which consist of a common local profile and opposite global corrections determined by a linear Neumann problem. Finally, we analyze two approximations to the Brenier map, namely the gradient of the dual potential and the conditional mean of the coupling. We obtain the sharp $L^p$ rate $\ell^{1+1/p}$ with exact leading constants and further identify the leading interior and boundary biases. Taken together, our results illustrate that quadratic regularization induces an accurate sparse approximation of classical optimal transport.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes quadratically regularized optimal transport with quadratic cost at small regularization ε, showing the optimal coupling is sparse and contains the Brenier map's graph, with explicit ellipsoidal local limits and sharp L^p approximation rates.
AI.motivation: Quadratic regularization is a popular computationally tractable approach to optimal transport, but its behavior in the small-regularization regime (sparse support, relation to the classical Brenier map) is not fully understood. The authors aim to characterize this regime precisely for smooth marginals.
AI.method: Asymptotic analysis of the regularized problem for smooth marginal densities in R^d. The support of the optimal coupling is studied after centering by the Brenier image and rescaling by ℓ=ε^{1/(d+2)}; dual potentials are expanded to order ℓ^2, with coefficients split into a common local profile and global corrections from a linear Neumann problem.
AI.result: The support contains the Brenier map's graph. After centering and rescaling by ℓ=ε^{1/(d+2)}, support sections have explicit ellipsoidal limits, except half-space profiles at boundary points. Dual potentials admit uniform expansions at order ℓ^2. Both approximations to the Brenier map (gradient of dual potential, conditional mean of coupling) achieve the sharp L^p rate ℓ^{1+1/p} with exact leading constants, including interior and boundary biases.
AI.conclusion: Quadratic regularization induces an accurate sparse approximation of classical optimal transport, with precise asymptotic geometry of the support and sharp approximation rates for the Brenier map.

title: Resonance expansions and local-energy decay estimates for Dirac operators
summary: We study resonance expansions and localised long-time dynamics for three-dimensional semiclassical Dirac operators. For smooth Hermitian matrix-valued perturbations which are analytic outside a compact set, we first obtain exponential cut-off resolvent bounds away from the resonance set and polynomial bounds in thin resonance-free rectangles adjacent to the real axis. Combining these estimates with a local $\Oc(h^{-3})$ upper bound on the number of resonances, a pigeonhole selection of admissible contours, almost-analytic functional calculus, and a Cauchy--Green deformation, we derive resonance expansions for spectrally localised propagators. Positive-energy resonances contribute for large positive times, whereas negative-energy resonances contribute for large negative times. We then specialise to mass-type perturbations $\mbfβV(x)$ in a nontrapping energy window.
