Using the logarithmic resonance-free region established in our earlier work together with a quantitative FBI-transform/escape-function argument, we obtain a polynomial bound for the continued cut-off resolvent and deduce rapid local-energy decay. We subsequently refine this polynomial estimate by a finite-time propagation argument in the undistorted region. Introducing the maximal positive-sheet connection time $T_χ$ associated with the spatial cutoff, we prove a geometric continued-resolvent estimate and, for every fixed $M$ below the resonance-free depth constant, derive the explicit local-energy decay threshold $T_N>T_χ+(N+1)/M$. The same analysis gives a rigorous microlocal obstruction to a uniform $[h\log(1/h)]^{-1}$ bound for the full distorted resolvent and identifies a finite-flight-time amplification mechanism for the sandwiched continued resolvent at logarithmic depth.

AI.tldr: The paper develops resonance expansions and long-time localised dynamics for 3D semiclassical Dirac operators, deriving resolvent bounds, resonance expansions for propagators, and explicit local-energy decay thresholds for mass-type perturbations.
AI.motivation: Understanding resonance expansions and long-time dynamics for semiclassical Dirac operators, particularly distinguishing positive- and negative-energy resonance contributions, and quantifying local-energy decay and resolvent behaviour for mass-type perturbations.
AI.method: Exponential cut-off resolvent bounds away from resonances and polynomial bounds in thin resonance-free rectangles; local O(h^{-3}) resonance-count bound; pigeonhole contour selection; almost-analytic functional calculus; Cauchy-Green deformation; logarithmic resonance-free region; quantitative FBI-transform/escape-function argument; finite-time propagation in the undistorted region; maximal positive-sheet connection time T_χ.
AI.result: Resonance expansions for spectrally localised propagators with positive-energy resonances contributing at large positive times and negative-energy at large negative times; polynomial continued cut-off resolvent bound and rapid local-energy decay; geometric continued-resolvent estimate and decay threshold T_N > T_χ + (N+1)/M; a microlocal obstruction to a uniform [h log(1/h)]^{-1} bound and a finite-flight-time amplification mechanism.
AI.conclusion: The analysis yields sharp resonance expansions, explicit local-energy decay thresholds, and identifies obstructions and amplification mechanisms for distorted and continued resolvents in semiclassical Dirac operators.

title: On Two Species Long Range Segregation in an Annular Domain
summary:
We consider a system of elliptic equations, depending on a small parameter $ε> 0$, which models the long range segregation of populations. The system has been previously studied in \cite{CL2} for the regularity of the free boundary in dimension $2$ and in \cite{ChPaTo26_2} and \cite{ChPaTo26_3} for the partial regularity of the free boundary in higher dimensions. In this paper, we consider the special case with $K = 2$ populations in an annular domain in arbitrary dimensions. Using the uniqueness and the rotational invariance of the solution, we show that the free boundary consist of concentric spheres. Moreover, by an application of the free boundary condition derived in \cite{CL2}, we show that the free boundary is uniquely determined. We also examine how the radius of the free boundary change according to the domain, the interaction distance and the boundary data. In particular, we show that the free boundary converges to that of the adjacent model as the interaction distance tends to zero.
  We also study the one parameter family of the elliptic system, in which the domain, the interaction distance, and the boundary data depends on $t$. We derive an ODE for the radius of the free boundary in dimension $2$ and dimension $n \geq 3$ separately. Several examples are given and discussed.

AI.tldr: An elliptic system modeling long-range segregation of K=2 populations in an annular domain is studied. Using uniqueness and rotational invariance, the free boundary is shown to consist of concentric spheres and is uniquely determined, with its radius depending on domain, interaction distance, and boundary data.
AI.motivation: Long-range segregation population models had prior work on free boundary regularity in dimension 2 and partial regularity in higher dimensions, but the special annular case with K=2 populations had not been analyzed in detail.
AI.method: Exploit uniqueness and rotational invariance of the solution for K=2 populations in an annular domain, apply the free boundary condition of prior work, and study a one-parameter family where domain, interaction distance, and boundary data depend on t.
AI.result: The free boundary consists of concentric spheres and is uniquely determined; its radius varies with domain, interaction distance, and boundary data, converging to the adjacent model's free boundary as interaction distance tends to zero. An ODE for the radius is derived separately for dimension 2 and n≥3, with several examples.
AI.conclusion: The special K=2 annular case admits a fully characterized concentric-sphere free boundary, offering explicit radius dynamics via ODEs and a convergence result to the adjacent model.

title: A Global Wavefront Set Condition for Defining Bony's Paraproduct Decomposition
summary: We establish a natural generalization of the Hörmander condition for the multiplication of Besov distributions using the global wavefront set framework of Coriasco, Johansson, and Toft. Using this condition, we relate the microlocal perspective on multiplication of distributions to the classical paraproduct decomposition of pointwise multiplication arising in the paradifferential calculus of Bony.

AI.tldr: The paper generalizes Hörmander's condition for multiplying Besov distributions via the global wavefront set framework, linking microlocal multiplication to Bony's paraproduct decomposition.
AI.motivation: Hörmander's condition governs when distributions can be multiplied, but it needed a natural generalization for Besov distributions. The authors aim to connect the microlocal (wavefront set) perspective on distribution multiplication with the classical paraproduct approach.
AI.method: They use the global wavefront set framework of Coriasco, Johansson, and Toft to establish the generalized Hörmander condition, then relate microlocal multiplication to Bony's paraproduct decomposition from paradifferential calculus.
AI.result: A natural generalization of the Hörmander condition for Besov distributions is established, and the microlocal perspective is tied to the paraproduct decomposition of pointwise multiplication.
AI.conclusion: The global wavefront set framework provides a unifying view connecting microlocal multiplication theory with paradifferential calculus.

title: An abstract averaging method for quasilinear equations
summary: We develop an abstract averaging method for equations $Mx=\varepsilon N(x,\varepsilon)$ in Banach spaces. The method applies when the equation can be separated into an averaged compatibility condition and a nonlinear complementary problem, and it allows the principal operator $M$ to be genuinely nonlinear. We prove that every nondegenerate zero of the corresponding averaged equation generates, for all sufficiently small nonzero values of $\varepsilon$, a nearby solution. Under a suitable small Lipschitz condition this solution is locally unique, while in the differentiable case it belongs to a unique local $C^1$ branch. The framework contains the abstract linear Fredholm averaging theory as a special case, but also covers quasilinear problems for which the principal operator has no invertible linearization at the reference state. We also determine the leading asymptotic profile of the solutions. Applications are given to a vector $p$-Laplacian Duffing system and to a nonsmooth problem in a Hilbert space.

AI.tldr: The paper develops an abstract averaging method for equations Mx=εN(x,ε) in Banach spaces where the principal operator M may be genuinely nonlinear, proving that nondegenerate zeros of the averaged equation generate nearby solutions for small ε, with applications to p-Laplacian Duffing systems and nonsmooth Hilbert space problems.
AI.motivation: Existing abstract averaging/Fredholm theory typically requires the principal operator to possess an invertible linearization at the reference state, restricting its use to semilinear-type problems and excluding genuinely nonlinear or quasilinear operators.
AI.method: The equation is split into an averaged compatibility condition and a nonlinear complementary problem, allowing M to be nonlinear. The authors prove existence of solutions near nondegenerate zeros of the averaged equation, establish local uniqueness under a small Lipschitz condition, obtain a unique local C1 branch in the differentiable case, and determine the leading asymptotic profile of solutions.
AI.result: Every nondegenerate zero of the averaged equation generates a nearby solution for all sufficiently small nonzero ε. Under a small Lipschitz condition the solution is locally unique; in the differentiable case it lies on a unique local C1 branch. The framework recovers abstract linear Fredholm averaging as a special case and extends to quasilinear problems without invertible linearization. Applications include a vector p-Laplacian Duffing system and a nonsmooth Hilbert space problem.
AI.conclusion: The proposed abstract averaging method generalizes classical linear Fredholm averaging theory to genuinely nonlinear principal operators, providing existence, uniqueness, regularity, and asymptotic profile results, with concrete applications to quasilinear and nonsmooth problems.

title: An averaging method for periodic solutions of quasilinear equations in Banach spaces
summary: The aim of the paper is to provide an extension of the averaging method to the periodic problem for quasilinear differential equations $(φ(t,u'))' = \varepsilon f(t,u,u',\varepsilon)$, $u(0) = u(T)$, $u'(0) = u'(T)$, where $u$ and $u'$ take values in a Banach space $X$ and $φ$ is a suitable homeomorphism between a neighborhood of $0$ in $X$ and $X$. The approach follows from a given extension of the averaging method to first order systems of the form $u' = g(t,v)$, $v' = h(t,u,v)$, $u(0) = u(T)$, $v(0) = v(T)$, in a product of Banach spaces, obtained from a direct application of the implicit function theorem in Banach spaces to an equivalent problem. We prove that every nondegenerate zero of the corresponding averaged equation generates, for sufficiently small nonzero values of the parameter, a unique nearby periodic solution. An application is given to an infinite system of coupled forced pendulums with relativistic acceleration.

AI.tldr: The paper extends the averaging method to periodic problems for quasilinear differential equations in Banach spaces, proving that nondegenerate zeros of the averaged equation yield unique nearby periodic solutions for small parameter values.
AI.motivation: The averaging method is a classical tool for studying periodic solutions, but its extension to quasilinear differential equations involving a homeomorphism φ in Banach spaces is not well established. The paper aims to fill this gap by developing such an extension.
AI.method: The approach extends the averaging method to first-order systems u' = g(t,v), v' = h(t,u,v) in a product of Banach spaces, derived via a direct application of the implicit function theorem in Banach spaces to an equivalent problem. This is then applied to the quasilinear equation (φ(t,u'))' = εf(t,u,u',ε) with periodic boundary conditions.
AI.result: It is proven that every nondegenerate zero of the corresponding averaged equation generates, for sufficiently small nonzero parameter values, a unique nearby periodic solution. An application is given to an infinite system of coupled forced pendulums with relativistic acceleration.
AI.conclusion: The averaging method can be successfully extended to periodic problems for quasilinear differential equations in Banach spaces, with the implicit function theorem providing the key tool, and the results apply to concrete physical systems such as coupled relativistic pendulums.

title: Control of 1D first-order linear hyperbolic systems: a brief survey
summary: At the occasion of the 70th birthday anniversary of Jean-Michel Coron, we review the literature on the control of 1D first-order linear hyperbolic systems, a topic where he has made significant contributions.

AI.tldr: A review of the literature on controlling 1D first-order linear hyperbolic systems, honoring Jean-Michel Coron's contributions on his 70th birthday.
AI.motivation: The occasion of Jean-Michel Coron's 70th birthday anniversary motivates this survey of a field where he made significant contributions.

AI.result: A synthesis of the literature on control of 1D first-order linear hyperbolic systems.

title: Minimal control time of some 1D first-order linear hyperbolic systems with row rank deficient boundary coupling matrix
summary: The minimal control time of one-dimensional first-order linear hyperbolic systems is by now well-known when the boundary coupling matrix is full row rank. The goal of this article is to characterize the minimal control time for a class of systems with row rank deficient boundary coupling matrices.

title: Edge-cusped compactons from gradient-power nonlinear dispersion: exact transitions and singular spectral structure
comment: 19 pages, 6 figures. Reproducibility code and numerical data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22671976
summary: We introduce a conservative two-exponent dispersive family, with $p>1$ the nonlinear-flux exponent and $r>0$ the gradient-dispersion exponent, that separates the mechanisms governing compactification, free-boundary regularity and linearised spectral structure while retaining an explicit travelling-wave theory. The family reduces to the absolute Rosenau-Hyman equation when $r=1$. The deformation leaves the amplitude-speed law unchanged, but makes the width amplitude dependent except at $r=1$. Two independent transition curves emerge: $pr=1$ separates infinite-tail solitary waves from compactons, whereas $r(p-1)=2$ separates compactons with a regular free boundary from edge-cusped compactons with divergent slope. The latter remain distributional solutions, with no singular measures at either the free boundary or the crest. For $r\ge1$, the linearisation factors through a singular Sturm-Liouville operator whose natural Friedrichs realisation is solvable: after a compacton-adapted change of variable, the eigenvalue equation is of Jacobi-hypergeometric type, with two explicit spectral sequences, exactly one negative eigenvalue and a one-dimensional translation kernel. Numerical experiments connect these exact structures to approximation and dynamics. Measured Fourier tails and projection errors agree with the rates predicted by the free-boundary exponent, while padded Fourier-Galerkin time integration propagates the cusped waves coherently with small phase drift. A structure-adapted Jacobi-Galerkin diagnostic of the full generator finds no detectable real part in the tested truncated point spectra. The family therefore provides an explicit testbed in which geometric singularity, weak admissibility, spectral structure and numerical regularity of compactons can be studied within a single degenerate dispersive model.

AI.tldr: A two-exponent dispersive compacton family (with exponents p, r) decouples compactification, free-boundary regularity, and spectral structure while keeping an explicit travelling-wave theory.
AI.motivation: Compactons (compact-support solitary waves) mix several phenomena—formation, edge regularity, and linearised spectra—that are hard to separate in existing models like Rosenau-Hyman. A tunable model is needed to isolate these mechanisms within one degenerate dispersive framework.
AI.method: Introduce a conservative two-exponent family with nonlinear-flux exponent p>1 and gradient-dispersion exponent r>0, reducing to absolute Rosenau-Hyman at r=1. Study travelling waves, transition curves, free-boundary behaviour and edge cusps; analyse linearisation via a singular Sturm-Liouville operator solved by a compacton-adapted change of variable giving a Jacobi-hypergeometric eigenvalue problem. Numerical tests use Fourier tails, projection errors, padded Fourier-Galerkin time integration, and a Jacobi-Galerkin spectral diagnostic.
AI.result: Amplitude-speed law is unchanged but width becomes amplitude-dependent except at r=1. Transition curves pr=1 (infinite-tail solitary waves vs compactons) and r(p-1)=2 (regular free boundary vs edge-cusped compactons) appear. Edge-cusped waves remain distributional solutions with no singular measures. For r>=1 the linearisation yields two explicit spectral sequences, exactly one negative eigenvalue and a one-dimensional translation kernel. Numerics confirm predicted tail/projection rates, coherent cusped-wave propagation with small phase drift, and no detectable real part in truncated point spectra.
AI.conclusion: The family offers an explicit testbed uniting geometric singularity, weak admissibility, spectral structure and numerical regularity of compactons in a single degenerate dispersive model.

title: The Heat Kernel of the Hodge Laplacian on an Invariant Subspace of 1-forms on the Hyperbolic Space $\mathbb{H}^{n}$
summary: In this paper, we construct explicit formulas for the heat kernel of the Hodge Laplacian restricted to an invariant subspace of $1$-forms on the real hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n}$. Using warped product decompositions, the problem is reduced to component operators on specific subspaces, yielding precise closed-form expressions for both odd and even dimensions. We further establish Millson-type recurrence relations that connect heat kernels across differing dimensions. Based on these explicit representations, we derive sharp uniform estimates and long-time asymptotic behavior, extending classical scalar heat kernel bounds to $1$-forms on real hyperbolic spaces.

AI.tldr: The paper derives explicit heat kernel formulas for the Hodge Laplacian on an invariant subspace of 1-forms on real hyperbolic space H^n, via warped product reductions, and uses these to obtain sharp uniform estimates and long-time asymptotics.
AI.motivation: Classical heat kernel bounds are well established for scalar functions on real hyperbolic spaces, but analogous sharp results for differential forms (Hodge Laplacian on 1-forms) are less developed. This work aims to extend such bounds to 1-forms.
AI.method: Restrict the Hodge Laplacian to an invariant subspace of 1-forms and use warped product decompositions to reduce it to component operators on specific subspaces, yielding closed-form heat kernel expressions in both odd and even dimensions. Millson-type recurrence relations connect heat kernels across dimensions.
AI.result: Explicit closed-form heat kernel expressions for odd and even dimensions, Millson-type recurrence relations across dimensions, sharp uniform estimates, and long-time asymptotic behavior for the 1-form heat kernel.
AI.conclusion: The paper extends classical scalar heat kernel bounds to 1-forms on real hyperbolic spaces, providing explicit representations and sharp analytic estimates.

title: Strict Log-Concavity of First Dirichlet Eigenfunctions under Symmetry in $\mathbb{CP}^n$
summary: We prove that the positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction of every smooth domain with convex boundary in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ invariant under the standard $U(1)\times U(n-1)$-action is strictly log-concave for $n=2,3,4$.

AI.tldr: Proves strict log-concavity of the positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction (invariant under the standard U(1)×U(n−1)-action) for smooth domains with convex boundary in CP^n, for n = 2, 3, 4.
AI.motivation: Log-concavity of first Dirichlet eigenfunctions is a classical and useful property, well studied in Euclidean space, but its analogue on complex projective space (and general Kähler manifolds) is less understood and of geometric interest.
AI.method: Analyzes the positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction restricted to the torus-invariant (U(1)×U(n−1)-symmetric) setting in CP^n, exploiting symmetry reduction and convexity of the boundary to establish strict log-concavity.
AI.result: The invariant positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction is shown to be strictly log-concave for smooth domains with convex boundary in CP^n when n = 2, 3, 4.
AI.conclusion: Establishes strict log-concavity for the U(1)×U(n−1)-invariant first Dirichlet eigenfunction in CP^n (n ≤ 4), extending Euclidean-type log-concavity results to complex projective space in low dimensions.

title: Inverse spectral results for the magnetic Schrödinger operator in low dimensions
summary: We consider the semiclassical magnetic Schrödinger operator in dimensions one and two. The first result is that an even one dimensional semiclassical potential is spectrally determined by the Schrödinger operator. The second result states that a two dimensional radial magnetic field is spectrally determined by a purely magnetic Schrödinger operator. This extends the earlier work of Guillemin-Wang and answers a conjecture of theirs therein.

AI.tldr: The paper proves spectral determination results for semiclassical Schrödinger operators: an even 1D potential and a 2D radial magnetic field are each uniquely determined by their spectra, extending Guillemin-Wang's work and resolving their conjecture.
AI.motivation: Guillemin-Wang previously studied spectral determination problems and posed a conjecture about magnetic Schrödinger operators; this work aims to extend their results and prove the conjecture in the purely magnetic 2D radial setting.
AI.method: Analysis of the semiclassical magnetic Schrödinger operator in dimensions one and two, using spectral invariants to recover the underlying potential (1D) or radial magnetic field (2D).
AI.result: An even one-dimensional semiclassical potential is spectrally determined by the Schrödinger operator; a two-dimensional radial magnetic field is spectrally determined by a purely magnetic Schrödinger operator.
AI.conclusion: The results extend Guillemin-Wang's earlier work and confirm their conjecture on spectral determination of radial magnetic fields.

title: The isoperimetric problem for four-dimensional parallelohedra
summary: We show that the regular $24$-cell uniquely minimizes surface area among four-dimensional parallelohedra of fixed volume. As a consequence, it also minimizes surface area among parallelohedra containing a fixed ball. Moreover, we establish quadratic Hausdorff stability, and we derive a second-variation formula valid across changes of Voronoi type, which identifies which root-lattice Voronoi cells are strict local minima under metric and affine perturbations.

AI.tldr: The regular 24-cell uniquely minimizes surface area among 4D parallelohedra of fixed volume, with quadratic Hausdorff stability and a cross-type second-variation formula.
AI.motivation: Surface-area minimization among parallelohedra is a geometric/tiling problem (related to Kelvin-type and Voronoi-tiling questions). The 4D case and the behavior across different Voronoi types were previously unresolved.
AI.method: Analytic geometry of parallelohedra and Voronoi cells: a second-variation (stability) formula that remains valid across changes of Voronoi type, plus Hausdorff-stability estimates.
AI.result: The regular 24-cell is the unique fixed-volume surface-area minimizer among 4D parallelohedra, and also minimizes area among parallelohedra containing a fixed ball. Quadratic Hausdorff stability holds, and the formula identifies which root-lattice Voronoi cells are strict local minima under metric and affine perturbations.
AI.conclusion: Provides a complete characterization of 4D surface-area-minimizing parallelohedra and a robust stability framework extending across Voronoi-type boundaries.

title: Bell-shaped functions are Poisson kernels
summary: In a recent paper [Kwaśnicki, Poisson kernels on the half-plane are bell-shaped, Bull. London Math. Soc. 58 (2026), no. e70303], the author proved that Poisson kernels for a class of elliptic operators in the half-plane are bell-shaped. By allowing one-sided barriers, we prove a converse result.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a converse of a recent result on bell-shaped Poisson kernels for elliptic operators in the half-plane, using one-sided barriers.
AI.motivation: Kwaśnicki (2026) proved that Poisson kernels for a class of elliptic operators in the half-plane are bell-shaped; this paper seeks a converse.
AI.method: The proof employs one-sided barriers.
AI.result: A converse to the bell-shaped Poisson kernel result is proved.
AI.conclusion: Allowing one-sided barriers yields a converse result, characterizing when Poisson kernels are bell-shaped.

title: The role of root allometry and root overlap in vegetation pattern formation
summary: We investigate how root allometry and below-ground root competition due to root overlap affect the conditions for pattern formation in non-local scalar vegetation models. We start from a spatially explicit two-component vegetation-water system in which plants acquire soil water through their laterally extended root systems, with root allometry represented by an interaction kernel whose spatial extent increases with the above-ground biomass density. In the limit of fast water dynamics, we eliminate the water variable, resulting in a non-local scalar model for the vegetation dynamics. This reduction reveals that accounting for root overlap naturally leads to a double integral structure in the scalar model, in contrast to the single convolution term commonly used to model non-local competition for resources. For the resulting scalar model, we identify two distinct mechanisms that can drive Turing instabilities. The first instability mechanism requires root growth to outpace mortality, while the second mechanism relies on the development of competitive pressure zones, in which vegetation growth is impeded by the cumulative competitive pressure exerted by neighbouring areas with higher biomass density. Root allometry promotes the occurrence of both instability mechanisms, while root overlap inhibits the emergence of competitive pressure zones. Hence, our results show that both root allometry and root overlap are important features to consider when studying vegetation pattern formation.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how root allometry and below-ground root competition (root overlap) shape pattern formation in non-local scalar vegetation models, showing both features are essential for Turing instabilities.
AI.motivation: Non-local vegetation models typically use a single convolution term for resource competition, ignoring root allometry (root extent scaling with biomass) and root overlap. The authors aim to capture these below-ground mechanisms more realistically.
AI.method: Starting from a spatially explicit two-component vegetation-water system with laterally extended root systems and biomass-dependent root allometry (interaction kernel), they take the fast-water limit to eliminate water, deriving a scalar non-local vegetation model. This reduction yields a double integral structure rather than a single convolution. They then analyze conditions for Turing instabilities.
AI.result: Two distinct Turing instability mechanisms are identified: (1) root growth outpacing mortality, and (2) development of competitive pressure zones where growth is impeded by cumulative competition from higher-biomass neighbours. Root allometry promotes both mechanisms, whereas root overlap inhibits competitive pressure zones.
AI.conclusion: Both root allometry and root overlap are important features that must be considered when studying vegetation pattern formation.

title: Quantum Optimal Transport Barycenters: Existence, Duality, and Gaussian Rigidity
summary:
We develop a Quantum Optimal Transport (QOT) barycenter framework for quantum states, as an analog of Wasserstein barycenters~\cite{AguCar}, and establish existence and duality results for a broad class of possibly unbounded transport costs on separable Hilbert spaces. Our framework provides, in particular, a unified treatment of $2$-quantum Wasserstein (QW) barycenters in both the quantum-state and quantum-channel formulations by specializing to the canonical quadratic cost operators associated with the $2$-quantum Wasserstein distances of Caglioti--Golse--Mouhot--Paul~\cite{caglioti2021towards,Golse-Mouhot-Paul:2016} and De Palma--Trevisan~\cite{DPaTre19}.
  The central results concern Gaussian input states and, in particular, Gaussian rigidity: whether Gaussian input states force the 2-QW barycenter itself to be Gaussian and uniquely determined when the minimization is taken over all quantum states. We first show that the barycenter problem admits a Gaussian minimizer and reduces to a finite-dimensional convex optimization problem over covariance matrices.
  The main difficulty is that uniqueness of the optimal covariance does not, in general, imply uniqueness of the underlying quantum state. We bridge this gap through a state-reconstruction principle under covariance complementary slackness that upgrades uniqueness of the optimal covariance to uniqueness of the full quantum state, and thereby prove a global rigidity theorem: if at least one Gaussian input is faithful, then the barycenter is unique among all quantum states and is necessarily Gaussian. Faithfulness is sufficient but not necessary: families of pure inputs still determine a unique barycenter, whereas partially pure nonfaithful Gaussian inputs may admit multiple barycenters.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a Quantum Optimal Transport (QOT) barycenter framework for quantum states, proving existence, duality, and Gaussian rigidity results for 2-quantum Wasserstein barycenters.
AI.motivation: Wasserstein barycenters are central in classical optimal transport, but a general theory for quantum states—covering existence, duality, and Gaussian rigidity—is lacking. The paper aims to build an analog for possibly unbounded transport costs on separable Hilbert spaces and unify existing 2-QW formulations.
AI.method: The authors introduce a QOT barycenter framework and specialize to quadratic cost operators underlying 2-quantum Wasserstein distances. They reduce the barycenter problem over all quantum states to a finite-dimensional convex optimization over covariance matrices, and use a state-reconstruction principle under covariance complementary slackness to upgrade covariance uniqueness to state uniqueness.
AI.result: Existence and duality results are established for broad (possibly unbounded) transport costs. The barycenter problem admits a Gaussian minimizer and reduces to convex optimization over covariances. Under complementary slackness, optimal covariances lift to unique full quantum states. A global rigidity theorem follows: if at least one Gaussian input is faithful, the barycenter is unique among all quantum states and is Gaussian.
AI.conclusion: Faithfulness is sufficient but not necessary for Gaussian rigidity: pure input families can still yield a unique barycenter, while partially pure nonfaithful Gaussian inputs may admit multiple barycenters. The framework unifies 2-QW barycenters in both state and channel formulations.

title: Stability and instability analysis of resonance-induced nonlinear bound states
summary: We study the focusing one-dimensional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger / Gross--Pitaevskii equation (NLS-GP), where the potential of the underlying linear Schrödinger operator, $H_V=-\partial_x^2+V(x)$, is compactly supported. In \cite{turner2026resonance} the authors proved that purely imaginary zeros (transmission resonances) or purely imaginary poles in the lower half plane (scattering resonances) of a reflection coefficient of $H_V$ seed branches of {\it resonance-induced nonlinear bound states}, and that these states bifurcate at a strictly positive $L^2(\mathbb R)$ excitation threshold. This is in contrast to nonlinear bound states which bifurcate at zero $L^2$-norm from point spectra of $H_V$ (corresponding to poles in the upper half plane). In this paper we establish precise criteria for the nonlinear orbital stability and instability of the resonance-induced states near the bifurcation point. A corollary is that resonance-induced nonlinear states are orbitally stable if i) the underlying linear (scattering or transmission) resonance frequency is sufficiently small, and ii) the corresponding linear resonance eigenmode is strictly positive. Numerical simulations are presented to explore regimes not accessible to our theory, and to explore the large time dynamics for initial conditions near stable and unstable resonance-induced nonlinear bound states.

AI.tldr: Establishes precise criteria for orbital stability/instability of resonance-induced nonlinear bound states in the focusing 1D cubic NLS-GP equation near the bifurcation point, with a corollary giving sufficient stability conditions and numerical simulations.
AI.motivation: Prior work (turner2026resonance) showed that purely imaginary resonances of a compactly supported potential seed resonance-induced nonlinear bound states bifurcating at a positive L2 threshold, unlike standard nonlinear bound states bifurcating at zero L2-norm. The stability properties of these resonance-induced states near bifurcation were not established.
AI.method: Analysis of the focusing 1D cubic NLS-GP equation with compactly supported potential in the linear Schrödinger operator; derive precise criteria for nonlinear orbital stability and instability near the bifurcation point; numerical simulations for regimes beyond the theory.
AI.result: Precise criteria for orbital stability and instability of resonance-induced states near bifurcation. Corollary: such states are orbitally stable if (i) the underlying linear resonance frequency is sufficiently small and (ii) the corresponding linear resonance eigenmode is strictly positive. Numerical simulations explore inaccessible regimes and large-time dynamics near stable/unstable states.
AI.conclusion: Resonance-induced nonlinear bound states can be orbitally stable under small resonance frequency and positive eigenmode conditions, providing a stability theory complementing the earlier bifurcation result, supported by numerical exploration of broader regimes.

title: Densities for scalar-valued BSDEs via unique continuation and backward uniqueness
summary: We give sufficient conditions ensuring that, at every fixed positive time, the scalar backward component of a Markovian forward-backward stochastic differential equation with multidimensional forward process admits a density with respect to Lebesgue measure. Existing density criteria for BSDEs often obtain Malliavin non-degeneracy through sign or monotonicity assumptions. We develop a different route for a scalar backward component with an arbitrary-dimensional forward state. Under regularity assumptions and a structural compatibility condition on the generator, the terminal condition is only required to be non-constant. The key idea is to deduce Malliavin non-degeneracy from deterministic rigidity of the critical set of the decoupling field. We combine Malliavin calculus with unique continuation and backward uniqueness for the associated semilinear parabolic equation. Unique continuation precludes the spatial gradient of the decoupling field from vanishing on a set of positive measure unless it vanishes identically on that time slice, while backward uniqueness propagates such vanishing to the terminal time. Along the way, we establish a unique continuation property from sets of positive measure and a backward uniqueness result on the whole space for the linear parabolic systems arising from differentiated semilinear equations.

AI.tldr: Sufficient conditions are given for the scalar backward component of a Markovian FBSDE (with multidimensional forward process) to have a density at every fixed positive time, based on Malliavin non-degeneracy derived from rigidity of the decoupling field's critical set.
AI.motivation: Existing density criteria for BSDEs typically obtain Malliavin non-degeneracy through sign or monotonicity assumptions. The authors seek a different route for a scalar backward component with an arbitrary-dimensional forward state.
AI.method: Under regularity assumptions and a structural compatibility condition on the generator (terminal condition only needs to be non-constant), Malliavin non-degeneracy is deduced from deterministic rigidity of the critical set of the decoupling field. This combines Malliavin calculus with unique continuation and backward uniqueness for the associated semilinear parabolic equation. Auxiliary results include a unique continuation property from sets of positive measure and a whole-space backward uniqueness result for linear parabolic systems from differentiated semilinear equations.
AI.result: The scalar backward component admits a density with respect to Lebesgue measure at every fixed positive time. Unique continuation prevents the spatial gradient of the decoupling field from vanishing on a positive-measure set unless it vanishes identically on that time slice, while backward uniqueness propagates such vanishing to terminal time.
AI.conclusion: Malliavin non-degeneracy for scalar BSDEs can be established via deterministic rigidity of the decoupling field's critical set, using unique continuation and backward uniqueness, avoiding classical sign/monotonicity assumptions.
